A regioselective synthesis of new mono and bisoxindoles containing bis spiro heterocyclic hybrids has been envisaged via 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of azomethine ylides with the corresponding diazo ester, obtained from a reaction of isatin with oxalylochloride. Some of the spiro compounds have got also the embedded pharacophore of 4-amino-piperidine, thus they are potential monoamine re-uptake inhibitors. The new spirooxindoles were submitted to biologic evaluation to evaluate the MAO-B inhibiting activity.

The 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition reaction between azomethine ylide and diazo ester gives a good yield of 62-98%, depending on the substitution of the isatin used in the reaction.

The structure of the spiro compounds was proved by MS and NMR.

Biologic evaluation of the new spirooxindols is made on 20 different samples and some of them have had a high MAO-B inhibiting activity and also a good absorption of the MAO-B inhibition, and this means that these spirooxindos can be possible drugs.

This paper presents comparisons between predicted and measured data for a live GSM system. Our propagation prediction software tool is based on 3D-ray tracing, and considers wave interactions, such as free space, reflection, diffraction, and scattering. The underlying propagation model uses a grid of grid points, placed at a 1 meter interval, in a 20m * 20m square around the base station. The measured data was done on one floor in a building. The floor above and below the measurement floor was empty. No people were present in the building during the measurement.

In the measurements, two antennas were used. The first was on top of the building (6m from the floor), at 15m away from the base station and the second was on the ground at 4m from the base station. 

We compared the predicted and measured data, and got  a good agreement between the RSSI values (Received Signal Strength)  for the first antenna, and for the 20 lowest power levels of the 2nd antenna. The higher power levels of the 2nd antenna was lower then the predicted power level. This was because these are the values when the signal is very strong and will not follow the radio-propagation rules in buildings, as there are not always walls between the cell and the base, so there will be a free path to the base. 

The signal attenuates after 6.5m  (free path) at -40dB or more, and the free path is used for the 6 first measurement points (first 6m) at the 2nd antenna.

Title: Effect of PT-Symmetric Operator on Cohe Under the Non-Markovian Environments

In this work, we mainly investigate effect of PT-symmetric operation on the dynamic behavior of the relative entropy of coherence for a two-level system within non-Markovian environments and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover cohe by utilizing optimal PT-symmetric operator. We consider a two-level atom in a non-Markovian dissipation environment, where the reservoir correlation time  $\tau$ is large, the influence of the PT-symmetric operation on the coherence of the two-level atom is discussed. Our results show that if we choose the parameter a in PT-symmetric operator as the following value

 $$a = -\frac{2\Gamma_{21}}{(\Omega -2i\Delta)\tau},  $$
 the cohe of the system will increase and our system can be regarded as a PT-symmetiric system and can be used to get the entangle state.
